summary_paraphrase: A girl on a long car trip with her parents keeps asking whether they have arrived; they point out goats and ostriches until they reach a town with an enormous hole, where her father explains that miners once dug there for diamonds; on the way home she wonders whether there are diamonds under her own house.

beats.function: 'are we there yet?' cycle: ostriches, empty road, almost
the hole and who made it
diamonds everywhere; can you see one?

characters.name: Khumo
characters.desire: to arrive; then to know who made the hole
characters.change: from impatience to wonder; ends asking about her own home

characters.name: teddy bear
characters.relation_to_protagonist: toy carried throughout; silent, fixed expression

characters.name: the miners
characters.relation_to_protagonist: people of the past, seen only in the picture

humor_notes: Light: the repeated 'are we there yet?' and the parents' patience; no jokes in the pictures.

repetition.description: the child's arrival question and the parents' 'not yet' reply recur across the trip, ending on 'almost' and then 'we are here'
repetition.why: a question every listener knows from car trips; the 'almost' variant counts down to arrival

repetition.description: single-word lines piled up in threes: counting ostriches; here, there, everywhere; three pick sounds
repetition.why: short joinable words and a count to follow on the picture

repetition.description: diamonds in the ground return as diamonds under her own house
repetition.why: carries the place home into the child's own world

notes: The car windows frame the landscape like pages; the view changes while the question stays the same.
The destination is named only on a road sign in the picture.
The history of the mine (men digging under a watching overseer) is only in the picture; the text gives only the sound of picks.
Two-colour line drawing; the hole is the only large solid dark shape, which gives it weight.

strengths: a familiar car-trip question used as the refrain and the countdown
a direct question that hands the reader a task on the picture
ends on the child's own question, carrying the trip home
weaknesses: the history behind the hole is left to the picture, so text-only reading loses who the miners were
little happens to Khumo; she observes and asks

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Gentle non-fiction trip. The picture of the miners hints at a hard labour history without words; a parent may be asked about it. Peak is wonder at research intensity 4 of 5, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
